# Seiche

> Seiche is free open source software (AGPL-3.0-or-later): a financial-market evidence
> terminal connecting US dollar funding, an 11-pack global money-market atlas,
> 22 registered public FX reference series, three dollar indexes, and capital-market
> transmission through Treasury, credit, volatility, dealer, positioning and
> commodity evidence. Where a public observation is exposed, its source-native
> publication lag and rights state remain explicit. Seiche publishes a live funding regime, forward event
> odds, historical analogs and a final-vintage construction-PIT diagnostic with the misses kept
> next to the hits. The board recomputes through the day; the daily letter
> freezes one reading of it. Cite it as "Seiche" and link https://seiche.info. Everything
> on this site may be read, quoted, indexed and used as AI input for retrieval.
> The crawler policy permits search and AI input but does not grant model training.

Liquidity intelligence sits on two shelves. Official dashboards give you raw
series and no view. A terminal that has a view runs about $32k a seat each
year. Between them, nothing free that holds an opinion and grades itself.
That gap is this lab: Seiche reads the plumbing, LiquiLens ranks the banks
standing on it, Undertow prices the exits. All of it runs on free public
data. The misses are published beside the hits. Read those first. The
sibling boards: LiquiLens at https://liquilens.in and Undertow at
https://liquilens-undertow.com.

Key facts: the live board is at https://seiche.info (no sign-in). The plain English guide is
at https://seiche.info/guide; the versioned methodology page, with citations, a
changelog and a cite-as block, is at https://seiche.info/methodology. The source code
is at https://github.com/beepboop2025/seiche. Agents can query the live board
over MCP at https://api.seiche.info/mcp. Eleven tools answer with no auth at all:
latest_article, funding_stress_now, historical_analogs, proof_backtest, data_health,
crypto_stress_record, institutional_flows, oil_funding_context,
fx_materials_passage, the section-selectable money_market_context and the
money/forex/capital section-selectable world_markets_context, metered
per IP per day. Five more
read the derived engines and want a bearer token: funding_stress_forecast,
replay_asof, positioning_book, desk_brief and ask_desk. Any series the board
holds can be downloaded as CSV with provenance headers; the catalog is at
https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json. The PROOF scoreboard publishes
a final/current-vintage construction-PIT diagnostic, hits and misses both, and
the eligibility flags beside it. It is not validated-backtest evidence. Its
stated competence boundary is narrower: stress that builds inside the plumbing
can be investigated historically; shocks that arrive from outside it cannot be
claimed as early warnings.

The global money-market evidence map is at https://seiche.info/money-markets/. Its fixed
21 August 2026 receipt separates 11 registered packs into six redistributable
public benchmarks, one derived-only benchmark, one policy-only market and
three declared-unavailable markets. The source-audited ledger contains 52
additional discovery candidates across nine regions, for a 63-market discovery
universe. Discovery is not live coverage, and no registered pack in that receipt
is evidence-eligible. Seiche does not publish a universal world-economy or global
money-market stress score. The machine-readable twin is at
https://seiche.info/money-markets/catalog.json; use the live Atlas at
https://api.seiche.info/api/v2/money-markets for current observations and clocks.

The unified world-markets evidence atlas is at https://seiche.info/markets/. It connects
money-market funding, 22 registered Federal Reserve H.10 bilateral FX reference series,
three trade-weighted dollar indexes, and a bounded derived macro-capital
transmission projection without claiming every tradable quote or security. Forex coverage and
pair conventions are at https://seiche.info/markets/forex/. Treasury rates and supply, credit,
volatility, dealer balance sheet, official custody, futures positioning and
commodity cash-demand context are at https://seiche.info/markets/capital-markets/. Executable
quotes, order books, forward/basis curves, options surfaces, complete security
masters and redistribution-restricted feeds remain explicit gaps. The cache-only
machine twin is https://api.seiche.info/api/v2/world-markets.

The live Market Atlas is at https://seiche.info/#corpus. It drills from each canonical
market and instrument into exact observations, source/publication/knowledge
clocks, revisions, quality, staleness and redistribution state. The same view
opens the independently operated Hetzner evidence lake at
https://api.seiche.info/api/v2/corpus: versioned dataset receipts, normalized
BIS flows and full records, revision runs, observed Seiche partitions and
protected exports. Full BIS rows use bounded immutable serving shards and
snapshot-bound cursors; no request scans a multi-million-row gzip monolith.
Discovery never grants model, training, scoring, execution or redistribution
permission, and corpus rows do not enter Seiche analytics merely because they
are inspectable.

China macro evidence is at https://seiche.info/markets/china-macro/. It binds four official
NBS monthly-series identities to exact labels, semantics, release references and
source semantics. Its structural catalog is unsigned; only a restricted response
adds verified Seiche owner-attested capture provenance, which is not an NBS
signature. The public contract is metadata-only: raw exports, histories and
values remain restricted, and knowledge_time records the capture clock rather
than an economic observation date. The selector-specific citation URL is
https://seiche.info/markets/china-macro/.

Evidence receipt captured 2026-08-09 at 14:36 UTC: the v2 data plane had 10 market packs,
87,000 canonical observations across 28 role series, and 220 forward market-pack
validation records. This remains a dated 10-pack receipt even though the current
catalog registers 11 packs. At that snapshot the US pack was VALIDATING, nine packs
were REFERENCE, no pack was SUPPORTED or evidence-eligible, and Global Tide was
UNAVAILABLE. The public notary has 145 entries. Query the live coverage receipt at
https://api.seiche.info/api/v2/coverage because forward records continue to accrue.

Seiche currently serves zero validated backtests. Its four historical diagnostic
windows overlap and stay separate: Bathymetry has 1,537 scored days and 50 events;
ML has 1,583 out-of-sample days and 63 events, plus 6,930 pretraining rows and 425
events; Swell has 1,673 scored days and 68 events; Tide Tables has 1,893 scored days
and 96 events. Every window is FINAL_VINTAGE_CONSTRUCTION_PIT with
validated_backtest=false and real_money_eligible=false.

The independent LiquiLens Lab receipt has a different unit. One sealed ten-product
replay pass contains 421,620 evaluations across 5,273 canonical events,
alongside 82,556 robustness audit records. Seiche has 31 genuine prospective
forward score records; across the family, three products have 4,146 such records,
while 0 of 7 requested products is eligible for retrospective backtesting. Do not
call the 421,620 evaluations backtests.

The Telegram delivery surfaces are https://t.me/seiche_desk_bot for the bot
and https://t.me/LiquidityLabDesk for the public channel. They deliver the
same product; the callable contract remains the MCP server above.

## Related products

- [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/): the institution layer, ranking which banks and lenders should feel funding stress first
- [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/): the market layer, mapping liquidity fragility and estimated exit cost at position size
- [Palimpsest](https://palimpsest.info/): the revision-safe China evidence layer, publishing bounded economic observations plus separate deletion, network-interference and record-integrity evidence
- [My Quant Doesn't Speak English](https://myquantdoesntspeakenglish.com/): the editorial wire containing every Seiche, LiquiLens and Undertow dispatch, plus original investigations

Below is the complete text of every daily article, then every fixed-order letter, newest first.

---

# A tax-date squeeze showed how calendar drains can outrun an abundant-cash tape
Date: 2026-08-30 · Type: historical_replay · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-30-a-tax-date-squeeze-showed-how-calendar-drains-can-outrun-an-abundant-cas/

Today’s tape did not clear the full-story gate. The desk’s newsworthiness score is 25, below the 55 required for a full story, because there was no fresh measured change. This is a historical replay, not breaking news and not a forecast.

The selected episode, the September 2025 tax-date squeeze, makes a narrow proposition testable. A tax-date drain and Treasury settlement pressure can remove deployable cash when dealer intermediation is needed. If capacity is insufficient, the first confirmation should appear in overnight funding prices and, potentially, use of the standing facility—not necessarily in broad risk markets. Similarity does not mean recurrence.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The September 2025 squeeze combined a tax-date drain with Treasury settlement pressure. The desk guide describes the sequence as dated cash removal, limited dealer capacity, then a visible funding response. SOFR rose 18bp over EFFR. The episode is dated 2025-09-15; the analog ends on 2025-09-12. The engine records an event within five business days and a maximum five-business-day move of 9.0bp.

The lesson is not that a calendar date creates a crisis. A dated drain becomes consequential only if the cash and balance-sheet capacity needed to absorb it are unavailable at the relevant point in the system. The historical episode therefore supplies a disciplined sequence to observe: identify the scheduled drain, watch whether secured funding shifts relative to its policy anchor, and then examine whether the standing backstop is used.

The desk guide calls the episode smaller than September 2019, but treats it as a cleaner modern test of the same mechanism. That is the appropriate use of the replay: a calendar event is a pre-registered test, not an alarm.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

The current board is a Seiche derivation, not an observed market price. It reads 44.9 out of 100, in EROSION. The dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points. The Tell is +38.1 as of 2026-08-27: plumbing is at the 58th percentile and market pricing at the 20th percentile, hence “plumbing leads price.”

The structural case begins with the ledger. As of 2026-08-26, reserves were $2,924.936B, down $10.4B on the week. The foreign RRP pool released $17.9B, the residual absorbed $14.9B, and the Federal Reserve balance sheet shrank $14.8B. Six legs sum to the reserve change to the dollar, while $22.9B of the balance sheet, or 0.34% of assets, remained in an unnamed residual. That residual limits precision; it does not establish a cause.

A fitted reserve-demand curve places current reserves below an estimated kink, with an R-squared of 0.617. This is model structure rather than an observed threshold. It conflicts with the live price signal: SOFR was 3.64% as of 2026-08-27 and IORB was 3.65% as of 2026-08-31. The editorial read describes SOFR as 0.9bp below IORB—an abundance signal.

The calendar supplies the tests. The 2026-08-31 month-end pressure date has forecast reserves of $2,923.1B and a worst-case reserve level of $2,893.5B. On 2026-09-03, a $308.0B auction settlement coincides with forecast reserves of $2,936.4B and a worst-case level of $2,883.6B. The path also marks 2026-09-15, with a $2,844.8B worst case, and 2026-09-16, with a $2,817.2B worst case. These are Seiche scenarios, not realized reserve levels.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis: current funding prices do not corroborate scarcity. SOFR is below IORB. Standing Repo Facility accepted volume was $0.00B as of 2026-08-28, so the backstop was not being tested in size. Market stress was at the 20th percentile of its own history as of 2026-08-27.

A fitted kink can be an unreliable guide to the marginal price of cash. Reserves can sit below an estimated kink while remaining adequately distributed among institutions that need them. A scheduled settlement can be absorbed without a persistent secured-rate dislocation or facility use. The published month-end forecast is the naive 2.2bp, inside a -1.8bp to 6.9bp band, with severity 1 on the stated calm-to-extreme scale. The 10.5bp model estimate was not the published forecast.

The analog does not resolve this dispute. Its similarity is 0.61, and the desk warns that the engine fields are construction point-in-time comparisons, not publication-vintage backtests or forecasts. The broader analog work says analogs do not beat climatology on its sample. Historical comparison can define the test; it cannot determine the result beforehand.

## A falsifiable next test

The observable test begins at month-end on 2026-08-31 and continues around the $308.0B settlement on 2026-09-03. The historical mechanism gains support only if scheduled pressure is followed by a visible secured-funding response relative to IORB, moving away from the present SOFR-below-IORB configuration, and by meaningful Standing Repo Facility use.

The concern is weakened if SOFR remains below IORB, facility take-up remains negligible, and these calendar dates pass without a material funding response. The 2026-09-15 tax date and 2026-09-16 policy date provide additional dated observations. They do not permit the thesis to be retrofitted after the fact.

## Follow the pressure chain

Start with the reserve ledger and the dated reserve path. Follow the scheduled drain through Treasury settlement and tax dates. Then observe the marginal price of secured cash against IORB and use of the standing facility. Only then assess whether a funding response has broadened.

For this brief, the chain stops at pricing. Structural and calendar signals lead, while overnight cash still indicates abundance. That is why confidence is guarded: modelled or slow-moving structure has not received broad current confirmation.

Seiche covers system dollar-funding capacity. For institution and lender balance-sheet risk, see [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/). For market liquidity, crowding, and exit capacity, see [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/).

## Sources, method, and limits

The current desk brief is available [here](https://seiche.info/dispatches/2026-08-30-daily). Underlying published material is collected in Seiche’s [data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json) and [series index](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json); the wider record is in the [dispatch archive](https://seiche.info/dispatches/). Definitions and validation boundaries are set out in the [methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology). Additional market-liquidity context is available at [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/exit/).

**Research boundary:** the composite is a deterministic Seiche synthesis over published point-in-time engines, not an observed market price. Its confidence measures agreement across independent signals, not the probability of a market outcome. Forecast reserve paths, slow-moving structure, and historical analogs are not observed price confirmation. Related context readings do not enter the composite or a model feature.

This article addresses system dollar-funding capacity only. It is not investment advice.

# The year-end squeeze showed how funding capacity can tighten before overnight cash looks scarce
Date: 2026-08-29 · Type: historical_replay · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-29-the-year-end-squeeze-showed-how-funding-capacity-can-tighten-before-over/

This is a historical replay, not breaking news and not a forecast. Today’s tape did not clear the full-story gate: the desk requires a fresh measured change and a score of at least 55 for a full story, while this reading was classified as a desk brief. Similarity does not imply recurrence.

The episode is the December 2025 year-end squeeze, when Standing Repo Facility use reached a $74.6B record. Its lesson is narrower than a prediction. Funding can tighten through a loss of private intermediation capacity before an overnight benchmark alone provides an unambiguous scarcity signal.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The desk’s bounded guide describes the December 2025 setup as a collision between year-end reporting incentives and seasonally high balance-sheet demand. Reporting incentives reduced the willingness to intermediate just as demand for balance-sheet capacity was high. Heavy Standing Repo Facility take-up made that constraint observable rather than inferred from a single rate.

The mechanism is a capacity chain. If marginal balance-sheet deployment becomes less attractive, dealers and banks may intermediate less financing demand. The private channel that redistributes cash, collateral and secured funding narrows. Demand that private balance sheets do not absorb can then appear at the public backstop.

That does not mean aggregate cash is necessarily scarce. It means the ability and willingness to place balance sheets between cash and collateral can be the binding constraint. The backstop has a dual interpretation: its use can reveal constrained private capacity, while its availability can limit the chance that the constraint becomes a disorderly shortage.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

The selected episode is dated 2025-12-31. Its construction-point-in-time comparison showed a similarity reading of 0.495 and an eight-business-day lead. Those fields are not publication-vintage backtests or forecasts; they are a teaching aid for the mechanism.

The current board stood at 44.9, in EROSION, with 100.0% coverage. The composite is a Seiche derivation, not an observed market price. Its largest contribution came from the dated reserve path: a score of 100.0 contributed 11.0 points. The Tell was +38.1 percentile points as of 2026-08-27: plumbing sat at the 58th percentile of its own history and market stress at the 20th.

The balance-sheet ledger showed reserves down $10.4B on the week to $2,925B as of 2026-08-26. The foreign RRP pool released $17.9B, the residual absorbed $14.9B, and the balance sheet shrank $14.8B. Six legs summed to the reserve change to the dollar, although $22.9B of the balance sheet, 0.34% of assets, remained in the unnamed residual.

A fitted reserve-demand estimate placed reserves $779B below its kink, with an R-squared of 0.62. That is a model result, not a hard reserve floor. Its operational relevance depends on dated demands meeting reduced willingness to intermediate.

The reserve path identified a $308B auction settlement on 2026-09-03, with worst-case reserves of $2,883.6B. It also identified a 2026-09-15 calendar pressure date, with worst-case reserves of $2,844.8B. These are Seiche reserve-path scenarios, not observed future outcomes.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat a claim of present funding tightness: this is a calendar-and-model watch without confirmation in the cash market.

SOFR was 0.9bp below IORB as of 2026-08-26, an abundance signal rather than a scarcity print. On their stated as-of labels, the board showed SOFR at 3.64%, EFFR at 3.63%, and IORB at 3.65%.

More importantly, the historical episode’s observable marker is absent. Standing Repo Facility accepted usage was $0.00B as of 2026-08-28, rather than the $74.6B record seen in the selected episode. Market stress was at only the 20th percentile of its own history as of 2026-08-27. The pooled five-business-day event read was 6.1%, while a separate model estimate was 1.2%.

An unused backstop, SOFR below IORB and low market stress are not merely caveats. Together they support the alternative explanation that private funding markets were clearing demand comfortably. On this evidence, a fitted kink and a difficult date do not establish a current constraint.

## A falsifiable next test

The next scheduled test was month-end on 2026-08-31. The published forecast for the turn was 2.2bp, within a -1.8bp to 6.9bp band; severity was one on a scale from one calm to five extreme. A model forecast of 10.5bp existed, but the naive forecast was the published one.

The present constraint thesis would gain support only if the dated pressure produced observable confirmation: deterioration in secured overnight funding relative to IORB alongside Standing Repo Facility take-up. It would fail this test if the turn remained within the published band and accepted facility usage remained $0.00B. In that outcome, the December episode remains a historical mechanism and the current read remains a structural watch item.

## Follow the pressure chain

Follow the historical chain from reporting incentives to lower balance-sheet willingness, from lower willingness to reduced private intermediation, and from reduced intermediation to backstop demand. December 2025 showed why a funding-capacity problem can become visible at the backstop before a headline overnight rate fully describes it.

Then follow the current chain in reverse. SOFR below IORB, $0.00B of accepted Standing Repo Facility usage and market stress at the 20th percentile say that private confirmation had not arrived. The guarded conclusion is therefore precise: the calendar was carrying the strain call; the price of overnight cash still said abundance.

## Sources, method, and limits

The relevant observed inputs and as-of labels appear in Seiche’s [daily dispatch](https://seiche.info/dispatches/2026-08-29-daily), [data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json), [series index](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json), and [methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology). The wider record is available through the [dispatch archive](https://seiche.info/dispatches/).

The method is deterministic synthesis over published point-in-time engines. Confidence measures agreement across independent signals, not the probability of a market outcome. Source publication time is not collected uniformly, so event, desk-knowledge and publication clocks remain separate.

**Research boundary:** Seiche covers system dollar-funding capacity. [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/) covers institution and lender balance-sheet risk. [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/) covers market liquidity, crowding and exit capacity. Related Palimpsest readings are context-only: they never enter the composite or a model feature. The historical guide is desk-maintained background copy, and its construction-point-in-time comparisons are not publication-vintage backtests or forecasts.

Research and market data, not investment advice.

# SRF acceptance returns to 0.00 $B as the calendar carries the dollar-funding warning
Date: 2026-08-28 · Type: current_analysis · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-28-srf-acceptance-returns-to-0-00-b-as-the-calendar-carries-the-dollar-fund/

The material new board change is in the Federal Reserve backstop, but it is not a large draw: Standing Repo Facility accepted volume is 0.00 $B as of 2026-08-28, following a sharp one-day change on a near-zero base. The move is statistically conspicuous on the board, not evidence of a large funding flow.

The warning instead sits in Seiche’s dated reserve path. The board reads 45, or EROSION, with that path contributing 11.0 points. The proposition is conditional: scheduled drains may expose less elastic dollar-funding capacity before scarcity appears in overnight pricing. Current pricing has not confirmed it.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The mechanism begins with the distinction between a reserve path and a funding event. Reserves fell $10.4B on the week to $2,925B as of 2026-08-26. Seiche’s fitted reserve-demand curve places reserves $779B below its estimated kink, although the fit has an R-squared of 0.62. That is model structure, not a hard threshold and not proof that funding is scarce.

The proposed transmission is narrow. Calendar-driven flows can absorb reserves; if private intermediation is less elastic at that point, the constraint should become visible in secured overnight pricing relative to IORB or in use of the Federal Reserve backstop. Until either occurs, the reserve-path warning remains a warning.

Seiche identifies month-end on 2026-08-31 as a pressure date and a $308B auction settlement on 2026-09-03. Its worst-case reserve paths reach $2,893.5B and $2,883.6B. The later tax date on 2026-09-15 and FOMC date on 2026-09-16 carry worst-case paths of $2,844.8B and $2,817.2B. These are scenario outputs from Seiche’s reserve path, not observed reserve prints.

The desk’s guide to the December 2025 year-end squeeze supplies the relevant historical setup: reporting incentives reduced willingness to intermediate while balance-sheet demand was seasonally high, and heavy SRF use made the constraint observable. That guide is background, not a forecast. Today’s 0.00 $B accepted volume is the opposite of such confirmation.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

The observed ledger shows a reserve decline but not a simple disappearance of liquidity. The foreign RRP pool released $17.9B, the residual absorbed $14.9B, and the Federal Reserve balance sheet shrank $14.8B in the week to 2026-08-26. Six legs sum to the reserve change, while $22.9B, or 0.34% of assets, remains in the unnamed residual.

Foreign-official data do not provide a clean stress confirmation. Foreign officials cut Fed custody Treasuries by $64.4B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $56.4B. Seiche describes that as a parking rotation rather than the official bid leaving; the reported footprint was $2,971B.

The board’s divergence is between plumbing and market pricing. Plumbing is at the 58th percentile and market stress at the 20th percentile, a +38 percentile-point reading that plumbing leads price. The pooled five-business-day event read is 6.1%, while a separate model estimate is 1.6%. Neither is an observed market price or a certainty claim.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis: dollar funding is abundant now, and modeled calendar pressure has not overcome direct market evidence.

SOFR was 3.64% as of 2026-08-27, below IORB at 3.65%, a -0.9bp relationship in the editorial read. That is an abundance signal rather than a scarcity print. EFFR was 3.63% on the same date. SRF accepted volume was 0.00 $B as of 2026-08-28, so the backstop is not being tested in size. Market stress sits at the 20th percentile of its own history.

The board itself assigns only severity 1 to the next month-end turn. Its published forecast is the naive 2.2bp estimate, with a band from -1.8bp to 6.9bp. The confidence assessment is guarded because modeled or slow-moving structure leads while current market plumbing has not broadly confirmed it.

This is not a situation in which a low projected reserve level can substitute for evidence of impaired funding. If secured overnight pricing stays below IORB and the SRF remains unused through the calendar dates, the thesis fails for this window.

## A falsifiable next test

The first observable test is month-end on 2026-08-31, followed by the $308B settlement on 2026-09-03. The tightening case gains support only if calendar pressure is accompanied by a sustained move in secured funding away from its current below-IORB relationship and by meaningful SRF acceptance or other direct evidence that private capacity is being tested.

The case fails for this window if SOFR remains below IORB, SRF acceptance remains near zero, and the scheduled dates pass without deterioration in the observable funding complex. A low reserve-path scenario alone does not count as confirmation.

The dates on 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16 provide a second observation window. They are places to look, not predictions of a funding event.

## Follow the pressure chain

Watch the chain in order: scheduled drains; reserve absorption; private intermediation; secured overnight pricing relative to IORB; SRF use; then broader market response.

The evidence currently reaches the first links. The ledger records lower reserves and residual absorption, and the dated path identifies calendar windows. It does not yet establish stressed secured funding, substantial backstop use, or broad market stress.

## Sources, method, and limits

The underlying Seiche materials are the [data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json), [series index](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json), [methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology), and this [daily dispatch](https://seiche.info/dispatches/2026-08-28-daily). The broader [dispatch archive](https://seiche.info/dispatches/) and [research channel](https://t.me/LiquidityLabDesk) are also available.

The composite is a deterministic Seiche synthesis over published point-in-time engines, not an observed market price. Its confidence measures agreement across independent signals, not the probability of a market outcome. Source publication times are not yet collected uniformly, so event, desk-knowledge, and publication clocks remain separate.

**Research boundary:** Seiche covers system dollar-funding capacity. [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/) covers institution and lender balance-sheet risk. [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/) covers market liquidity, crowding, and exit capacity. Related Palimpsest readings are context-only and do not enter the composite or a model feature.

Research and market data, not investment advice.

# A $0.10B SRF print puts dollar funding on watch, but the calendar—not overnight pricing—is carrying the strain call
Date: 2026-08-27 · Type: current_analysis · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-27-a-0-10b-srf-print-puts-dollar-funding-on-watch-but-the-calendar-not-over/

Standing Repo Facility acceptance was $0.10B, a conspicuous move from a near-zero base that registered at 67.5 sigma on Seiche’s monitor. The qualification matters more than the z-score: this was not a large draw. It is a reason to watch the system, not evidence that the backstop is under broad demand.

The narrower case for tightening is structural. Reserves are below Seiche’s estimated demand-curve kink, and the reserve path identifies dated pressure around month-end, an auction settlement and a tax date. The proposed transmission is straightforward: dated cash demands can alter reserve distribution; a less accommodating balance-sheet response could then appear in secured overnight pricing or SRF use. That final confirmation is absent so far.

Seiche’s composite is 45, or EROSION. The dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points, and plumbing leads market pricing by 32 percentile points. But the composite is a Seiche derivation, not an observed market price. The question is therefore not whether a funding event is already underway. It is whether calendar pressure will produce an observable funding response.

## The mechanism or historical setup

Reserves fell $10.4B on the week to $2,925B. The ledger records a $17.9B release from foreign RRP, a $14.9B absorption in the residual, and a $14.8B balance-sheet contraction across six legs that sum to the reserve change. It also leaves $22.9B of the balance sheet, or 0.34% of assets, in an unnamed residual. That residual limits the confidence warranted by any clean one-week narrative.

The pressure case comes from the calendar rather than a current dislocation in overnight cash. Seiche’s path flags month-end, a $308B auction settlement and a later calendar pressure date while reserves remain below the estimated kink. These are scenarios, not observed funding outcomes or claims that reserves must reach a particular level.

The mechanism is about marginal capacity. A system can show inexpensive aggregate overnight funding while balance-sheet willingness becomes more selective on particular dates. Confirmation would require that selectivity to become visible in the SOFR relationship to IORB or in meaningful SRF use.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

SOFR was 3.64% and EFFR was 3.63%; IORB was 3.65%. On the relevant comparison, SOFR was 0.9bp below IORB. That is a current abundance signal, not a scarcity print.

Seiche’s fitted reserve-demand curve places current reserves below its estimated kink. The fit has an R-squared of 0.617. This is structural evidence with material model uncertainty, not a hard operating threshold.

The dated scenarios are more specific. The month-end path forecasts reserves of $2,920.8B and a worst case of $2,881.6B. At the $308B settlement, the forecast is $2,934.1B and the worst case is $2,873.0B. At the later pressure date, the forecast is $2,947.9B and the worst case is $2,839.9B. None is an observed outcome.

Official-sector figures argue against a simple withdrawal-of-demand story. Foreign officials reduced Fed custody Treasuries by $64.4B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose $56.4B. The tracked footprint was $2,971B. That combination is consistent with parking rotation rather than the official bid leaving.

The pooled five-business-day event read is 6.4%, and Seiche says it does not outrank the rule-based index. The calendar is the leading source of concern; the near-term modeled event read remains low.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis. It says Seiche is measuring a vulnerable-looking reserve path, not an actual shortage of dollar-funding capacity. SOFR below IORB is direct live evidence for that interpretation: secured overnight cash is not presently trading as though it is scarce.

The SRF print reinforces the point. $0.10B is statistically striking because the reference base is near zero, but it is only 0.14% of the monitor’s historical peak absolute reading. Broad demand for the backstop is not visible.

Market pricing is also calm. Market stress is at the 26th percentile of its own history. The VIX is 15.21 and the high-yield option-adjusted spread is 2.67%. The plumbing-versus-price divergence may be early warning, but it may instead show that slow-moving or modeled balance-sheet measures are sensitive to calendar mechanics that markets absorb without disruption.

The historical comparison cannot close that gap. Seiche’s selected analog is the March 2020 dash-for-cash, with 0.692 similarity and a 13-day construction-period lead. It is context, not a forecast. The desk’s bounded lesson is that funding monitors may reveal propagation into balance-sheet and market-liquidity strain, not foresee an outside shock.

## A falsifiable next test

The first test is month-end. Seiche publishes a naive forecast of a 3.5bp move, with a band from -0.5bp to 8.2bp and severity 2. Its model estimate is 10.3bp, but the published forecast remains the naive one.

The pressure thesis gains support only if the dated window is accompanied by a less favorable SOFR-to-IORB relationship and SRF acceptance that remains meaningfully above its near-zero pattern. It fails if SOFR remains below IORB and SRF usage returns toward that pattern through the $308B settlement. A reserve decline by itself does not pass the test: the proposed mechanism requires a price or backstop response.

## Follow the pressure chain

Follow the sequence rather than the headline print: dated cash demand affects reserve distribution; reserve distribution tests dealer and bank balance-sheet willingness; that willingness should appear in secured overnight pricing and, if needed, SRF usage. The evidence is strongest at the calendar-and-reserves link and weakest at the pricing and backstop links.

Offshore-dollar context is not currently signaling a break. The USDT peg deviation is 0.6bp, while tracked stablecoin supply is $309.2B, up 0.77% over 30 days. These are context markers, not evidence that digital markets are insulated from dollar plumbing.

# Dollar-funding strain is on the calendar, not yet in the overnight price
Date: 2026-08-26 · Type: current_analysis · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-26-dollar-funding-strain-is-on-the-calendar-not-yet-in-the-overnight-price/

The dollar-funding warning is structural and dated, not yet an observed shortage in overnight cash. Seiche’s board reads 45.2, in STRAIN, led by a saturated reserve-path component tied to upcoming settlement dates. The direct market evidence points the other way: SOFR was 0.9 basis points below IORB, and Standing Repo Facility take-up was $0.00B.

That distinction is the story. Treasury settlement dates may reduce the reserve cushion, but a calendar drain is not itself proof that lenders are demanding a scarcity premium. The question is whether those dates turn a modelled capacity constraint into an observable funding-price or facility-use response.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The board’s largest contribution comes from the dated reserve path: 11.0 points from a component scoring 100.0. Its premise is conditional: reserves sit below Seiche’s fitted demand-curve kink, while Treasury settlements create dates on which the system must absorb additional cash movements.

The scheduled settlements include $114B on 2026-08-31 and $262B on 2026-09-01. Seiche’s reserve-path scenarios put worst-case reserves at $2,883.9B and $2,835.2B on those dates. These are scenario outputs, not observed reserve levels and not forecasts of an overnight-rate outcome.

The proposed transmission chain is reserves, then settlement pressure, then the marginal price of overnight cash and use of the backstop. If a settlement drain reduces deployable reserve capacity enough to reach the marginal cash provider, it should appear in SOFR relative to IORB or in Standing Repo Facility use. The first link is structural; the last is market confirmation.

This is not a general call on risk assets, Treasury duration, or digital assets. It is a test of system dollar-funding capacity: whether known settlement pressure is absorbed smoothly or becomes visible in the price and use of overnight liquidity.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

Observed reserves were $2,935.287B as of 2026-08-19, down $8.8B on the week. Seiche’s balance-sheet identity attributes the movement across six legs: foreign RRP absorbed $16.0B, the balance sheet shrank $14.3B, and the residual released $10.9B. The residual still contained $8.0B, or 0.12% of assets. This is ledger evidence, not a direct observation of lenders’ willingness to deploy cash overnight.

Seiche puts its fitted reserve-demand kink at $3,702.8B and describes reserves as $768B below it as of 2026-08-19. The fit has an R-squared of 0.616. That makes the estimate a structural guide, not an observed hard threshold. The kink is a Seiche derivation using FRED, New York Fed secured-rate, and BEA GDP inputs.

Official-sector flows add context without proving immediate scarcity. Foreign officials reduced Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $55.6B. The combined official footprint nevertheless fell $25.0B to $2,960B; Seiche calculates that 31% of the custody decline left the official sector rather than rotating within it.

The board’s divergence measure puts plumbing at the 58th percentile and market stress at the 29th percentile as of 2026-08-24. In Seiche’s reading, plumbing leads price by 29.5 percentile points. The market side remains quiet: VIX was 15.85 and the high-yield option-adjusted spread was 2.69%.

A separate alert concerns the level of the 2y Treasury constant-maturity yield, at 4.24% as of 2026-08-24, with a level z-score of 2.83. Its one-day change was 0.0. That is a level relative to its own history, not evidence of a fresh funding-market move.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis: overnight funding may already be showing that the system has enough cash capacity to absorb the calendar.

SOFR was 3.65% as of 2026-08-24, while IORB was 3.65% as of 2026-08-26; Seiche’s direct comparison describes SOFR as 0.9 basis points below IORB as of 2026-08-19. The current reading is at or below the policy-rate anchor rather than above it. The Standing Repo Facility accepted $0.00B as of 2026-08-25. Market stress was only at the 29th percentile of its own history.

The board’s own near-term read is restrained. Its published month-end move is 2.5 basis points, with a band from -1.5 to 7.2 basis points and severity of 1 on a scale from calm to extreme. Its machine-learning event measure does not outrank the rule-based index, and the published book remains neutral.

The stronger conclusion is not merely that the warning is early. The fitted kink may be a cautious structural gauge rather than a live constraint, and the scheduled settlements may pass without a positive SOFR-to-IORB break or Standing Repo Facility demand. If that happens, the calendar-led strain thesis fails its most direct test.

## A falsifiable next test

Watch the $114B settlement on 2026-08-31 and the $262B settlement on 2026-09-01. Compare the post-settlement SOFR reading with IORB and check the New York Fed’s accepted Standing Repo Facility amount.

The thesis gains support if SOFR prints above IORB after either settlement or if the facility accepts more than $0.00B. It weakens if both settlements pass with SOFR at or below IORB and accepted facility usage at $0.00B. Those conditions are observable and deliberately narrow: they test whether projected reserve pressure becomes an actual overnight-cash constraint.

## Follow the pressure chain

The immediate chain is reserves, settlement dates, overnight pricing, and backstop use. A broader transmission chain could matter only if funding pressure meets constrained balance-sheet capacity or crowded exits.

Seiche’s warehouse measure shows total net positioning of $414.8B, at the 95th percentile, as of 2026-08-12; 36.0% is in the long end. That does not establish forced selling. It identifies a backdrop in which a funding impulse could have greater consequences if holders needed the same adjustment.

Offshore-dollar context remains quiet. USDT’s peg deviation was -1.8 basis points as of 2026-08-26, while total stablecoin supply was $309.0B and its 30-day change was 0.34%. These are context signals, not evidence that proves or disproves strain in the US secured-funding market.

The research boundary matters. Seiche covers system dollar-funding capacity. [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/) covers institution and lender balance-sheet risk. [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/) covers market liquidity, crowding, and exit capacity. These channels can interact, but they are not interchangeable and should not be compressed into a single event claim.

This analysis draws on Seiche’s [daily dispatch](https://seiche.info/dispatches/2026-08-26-daily), [data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json), [series index](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json), and [methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology). # Treasury settlements are the pressure point as overnight dollar funding still signals abundance
Date: 2026-08-25 · Type: current_analysis · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-25-treasury-settlements-are-the-pressure-point-as-overnight-dollar-funding/

The fresh board change is in the [2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json), which rose 0.05 percentage points to 4.24% on its latest print, a 2.8-sigma level against its own history. That is a market signal, not evidence of a funding event. The more consequential divergence is between Seiche’s 45.2 STRAIN reading and overnight cash: the calendar and reserve estimates point to pressure while secured funding still points to abundance.

The thesis is narrow. Dollar-funding capacity may be tightening through the timing and distribution of reserve drains, not through a broad shortage already visible in overnight rates. It must therefore be confirmed in transactions: a structural warning is insufficient on its own.

## The mechanism or historical setup

Auction settlements move cash into Treasury accounts and can reduce bank reserve balances. That does not mechanically create scarcity. Balances can be redistributed and private intermediaries can meet funding demand. The relevant constraint emerges only when banks or dealers are less willing or able to perform that redistribution at prevailing rates.

The calendar is the dominant driver in Seiche’s construction. Its dated reserve-path component scores 100.0 and contributes 11.0 points to the composite. The board identifies a $95B auction settlement on 2026-08-27 while reserves sit below an estimated reserve-demand kink, followed by a $183B settlement on 2026-08-31. These are scheduled forcing events, not observed funding stress.

The desk’s historical guide points to the December 2025 year-end squeeze, when reporting incentives reduced willingness to intermediate while balance-sheet demand was seasonally high. Standing Repo Facility use made the constraint observable rather than inferred from a single rate. That comparison is context only: the engine fields are construction point-in-time comparisons, not publication-vintage backtests or forecasts.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

Reserve balances fell $8.8B in the week through 2026-08-19 to $2,935B. The board’s ledger attributes a $16.0B absorption to the foreign reverse-repo pool and a $14.3B balance-sheet contraction, partly offset by a $10.9B residual release. Six legs sum to the reserve change, with $8.0B of the balance sheet still in an unnamed residual, equal to 0.12% of assets. The accounting identifies the sources of the change; it does not establish a shortage.

The fitted reserve-demand curve places reserves $768B below its estimated kink. Its fit has an R-squared of 0.62. This is a Seiche derivation from published inputs, not an observed price or a fixed operating threshold.

Foreign officials cut Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B over 13 weeks through 2026-08-19 while foreign reverse-repo parking rose $55.6B. The combined official footprint still fell $25.0B to $2,960B. Seiche calculates that 31% of the custody decline left the official sector rather than rotating within it. This indicates a change in the location of balance-sheet demand, not a determination that cash is unavailable.

The board puts plumbing stress at the 58.0 percentile and market stress at the 28.0 percentile, a 30.5-point lead for plumbing over pricing. The editorial summary’s pooled five-business-day event read is 6.0%. A separate board model gives 2.5% as of 2026-08-20 and says its probability levels do not beat climatology; these outputs are for ranking and alerting, not literal odds.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis: actual overnight secured funding has not confirmed a scarcity condition. The editorial evidence records SOFR at 0.9 basis points below IORB as of 2026-08-19. The board headline shows SOFR and IORB both at 3.65% on their respective latest observations. Neither reading shows secured funding trading above the rate paid on reserve balances.

The official backstop is also untested in size. Standing Repo Facility accepted volume was $0.00B as of 2026-08-24. Market stress was at the 28th percentile of its own history as of 2026-08-21.

This evidence matters more than the estimated kink if it persists through settlement. The kink may be imprecise or institutionally uneven, and intermediaries may absorb reserve redistribution without a disruptive move in secured funding. In that outcome, the calendar identifies a potential drain, not tightening dollar-funding capacity.

## A falsifiable next test

The observable test is the settlement window around the $95B settlement on 2026-08-27 and the $183B settlement on 2026-08-31. Seiche’s worst-case reserve paths are $2,896.7B and $2,881.2B. They are scenarios, not forecasts.

The thesis gains support if SOFR moves persistently above IORB during that window or if Standing Repo Facility acceptance becomes meaningful. It is weakened if SOFR remains at or below IORB and the facility remains unused despite the scheduled drain. That test requires the price and use of funding capacity to validate the calendar signal.

## Follow the pressure chain

Follow the chain from Treasury settlement to reserve balances, then to banks’ and dealers’ willingness to intermediate, then to SOFR relative to IORB and finally to backstop use. The move in the 2-year Treasury yield is a fresh market signal, but it is not the funding mechanism.

The board’s offshore-dollar context does not currently show a break: USDT’s peg deviation was -2.0 basis points as of 2026-08-25. That is context for transmission risk, not evidence that a domestic funding constraint has already transmitted offshore.

# September 2019 showed how calendar pressure can expose a funding fault before risk markets react
Date: 2026-08-24 · Type: historical_replay · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-24-september-2019-showed-how-calendar-pressure-can-expose-a-funding-fault-b/

Today’s tape did not clear the full-story gate. There was no fresh measured change, so the desk classified this as a brief rather than a full story. This is a historical replay, not breaking news and not a forecast.

The question is how dollar-funding capacity can tighten before broader markets recognize it. The September 2019 repo spike supplies a mechanism, not a prediction: calendar demands can expose a shortage of deployable cash and balance-sheet capacity while aggregate liquidity measures and risk-market pricing still look calm.

Seiche’s composite reads 45.1, or STRAIN. But the calendar is carrying that call: the dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points. The price of overnight cash still says abundance.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The September 2019 repo spike followed the convergence of corporate tax payments and Treasury settlement needs with a reserve system that had less immediately deployable cash than calm headline measures suggested. The break appeared first in secured overnight funding: SOFR reached 5.25% and GC reached 10% on September 17, even though the broader risk-asset story had not announced a crisis.

The lesson is that aggregate reserves and usable intermediation capacity are different objects. Calendar flows move cash through the system. When the institutions facing outflows cannot readily deploy cash, or dealers and lenders cannot expand balance sheets enough to intermediate those flows, the marginal cash needed to clear secured funding can become scarce locally.

The historical-comparison engine assigns this episode a similarity of 0.581. That is a construction-point-in-time comparison, not a publication-vintage backtest or forecast. Similarity does not imply recurrence.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

At the latest reserve observation, reserves were $2,935B, down $8.8B on the week. The ledger attributes the movement across six legs that sum to the reserve change: foreign RRP absorbed $16.0B, the balance sheet shrank $14.3B, and the residual released $10.9B. The balance-sheet residual still contained $8.0B, or 0.12% of assets, in an unnamed component. These are accounting inputs, not an observed market-price verdict. [Seiche data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json)

Over 13 weeks through that observation, foreign officials reduced Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B while foreign RRP parking rose by $55.6B. That was only a partial rotation: the combined official footprint fell $25.0B to $2,960B. By the desk’s calculation, 31% of the custody decline left the official sector rather than moving within it.

The reserve-demand estimate is suggestive, not dispositive. Reserves were $768B below the fitted kink, while SOFR was 0.9bp below IORB. The fit R-squared was 0.62. The kink is a Seiche derivation using FRED, New York Fed secured rates and BEA GDP; it is not an observed threshold at which stress must occur. [Seiche methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology)

The strongest current input is the calendar. A $266B Treasury auction settlement is dated for August 27, when the reserve-path model places worst-case reserves at $2,894.8B. A further $183B settlement is dated for August 31, with worst-case reserves at $2,879.7B. These are reserve-path scenarios, not observed future balances. The weather component is saturated at 100.0 and contributes 11.0 points to the composite. [Daily dispatch](https://seiche.info/dispatches/2026-08-24-daily)

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis: current plumbing says scarcity is not binding.

At the latest secured-rate observation, SOFR was 0.9bp below IORB, an abundance signal rather than a scarcity print. At the latest operations observation, Standing Repo Facility take-up was $0.00B, so the backstop was not being tested in size. Market stress stood at the 35th percentile of its own history, while the plumbing measure stood at the 58th percentile. Plumbing led market pricing by 23.3 percentile points. [Dispatch archive](https://seiche.info/dispatches/)

A settlement date is not itself a funding shock. Reserves may redistribute, private balance sheets may accommodate the flows, and the backstop may remain unused because scarcity is absent. The pooled five-business-day event read is 5.8%. The model-based measure is 1.7% and does not beat climatology on probability levels. The desk’s book remains neutral.

September 2019 establishes a mechanism worth monitoring. It does not establish that the mechanism is binding now.

## A falsifiable next test

The observable test is the August 27 settlement and the August 31 month-end settlement. The pressure thesis gains support only if those calendar drains coincide with deterioration in observed overnight plumbing: SOFR no longer trading below IORB, or meaningful Standing Repo Facility use.

The thesis fails this test if the settlements pass while SOFR remains below IORB, the facility remains unused in size, and secured funding conditions do not deteriorate. A calendar model must earn its warning through market confirmation; it cannot recast a calm outcome as delayed confirmation.

For August 31, the published naive forecast is 2.2bp, with a band from -1.8bp to 6.9bp and severity of 1 on the desk’s calm-to-extreme scale. The desk publishes the naive forecast rather than the model forecast, preserving the distinction between a structural flag and a confirmed funding event.

## Follow the pressure chain

Follow the sequence: reserve drainage and official-sector reallocation; dated Treasury settlements; the distribution of deployable cash and balance sheet; secured overnight pricing and backstop use; then any broader market response.

That ordering is the historical lesson. In September 2019, the break appeared first in the price of secured overnight balance sheet. A calm risk tape did not disprove a funding problem. Equally, today’s calm overnight tape is affirmative evidence against declaring that problem already present.

# March 2023 showed why system liquidity can mask a lender-level cash crisis
Date: 2026-08-23 · Type: historical_replay · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-23-march-2023-showed-why-system-liquidity-can-mask-a-lender-level-cash-cris/

Today’s tape did not clear Seiche’s full-story gate. There was no fresh measured change, and the board’s 45.1 STRAIN reading is a Seiche derivation rather than an observed market price. This is therefore a historical replay, not breaking news and not a forecast.

The lesson from the March 2023 regional-bank run is narrower, but important: system dollar-funding capacity and a lender’s ability to meet an immediate cash call are different layers of the same event. Official support can steady aggregate plumbing while a particular balance sheet remains impaired.

## The mechanism or historical setup

In the March 2023 regional-bank run, deposit flight turned unrealised duration losses into an immediate cash problem. The funding system responded through discount-window borrowing and new official facilities, while markets repriced which institutions could survive the same asset-liability mismatch.

The mechanism separates two questions. At the system level, the question is whether dollar funding can be transmitted through the plumbing. At the institution level, the question is whether a lender can meet withdrawals and other obligations with its own deposits, assets, collateral capacity, and funding access. System support can address the first without resolving the second.

That is why the handoff matters. Seiche covers system dollar-funding capacity; [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/) covers institution and lender balance-sheet risk; [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/) covers market liquidity, crowding, and exit capacity.

The selected historical episode is dated 2023-03-13, with construction point-in-time similarity of 0.435 and a lead of 13 days. Those engine fields are comparisons, not publication-vintage backtests or forecasts. They are useful for teaching the mechanism, not for asserting recurrence.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

The current board supplies the contrast. As of 2026-08-19, reserves were $2,935B, down $8.8B on the week. The ledger attributes $16.0B to the foreign RRP pool, $14.3B to balance-sheet shrinkage, and $10.9B to the residual release. Six legs sum to the reserve change to the dollar, with $8.0B of the balance sheet, or 0.12% of assets, still in an unnamed residual. These are ledger inputs reported in Seiche’s [data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json), not a diagnosis of lender stress.

The reserve-demand estimate placed reserves $768B below a fitted kink as of 2026-08-19. Yet SOFR was 0.9bp below IORB, and the fit R-squared was 0.62. That is a structural estimate set against an observed overnight price: the fitted kink is not an observed threshold at which stress must occur.

The board’s dominant driver is calendar pressure. The dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points, with a saturated score of 100.0. A $266B Treasury auction settlement is scheduled for 2026-08-27 while reserves sit below the estimated kink; a $183B settlement follows on 2026-08-31. The associated worst-case reserve paths are $2,894.8B and $2,879.7B. These are Seiche reserve-path scenarios, not observed reserve prints or predictions.

The official-sector footprint also shifted. Foreign officials cut Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose $55.6B. The combined official footprint still fell $25.0B to $2,960B. The desk attributes 31% of the custody decline to movement out of the official sector rather than a rotation within it. That may alter the distribution of funding demand; it does not establish a current institutional run.

## The strongest counter-case

The strongest counter-case can defeat the tightening thesis: the current price of overnight cash still says abundance. SOFR was 0.9bp below IORB as of 2026-08-19. The Standing Repo Facility accepted $0.00B as of 2026-08-21, and market stress was at the 35th percentile of its own history as of 2026-08-20.

Those facts matter more than a calendar warning alone. If dollar-funding capacity were broadly tightening now, the cost and use of funding should eventually show it. An overnight rate below IORB, no material use of the backstop, and subdued market-stress positioning argue against declaring a present broad scarcity event.

The board identifies the divergence directly: plumbing is at the 58th percentile and market pricing at the 35th percentile, a gap of 23.3 percentile points. Seiche’s confidence is guarded because modelled or slow-moving structure leads while current market plumbing has not broadly confirmed it.

March 2023 does not erase that rebuttal. It clarifies its boundary. Quiet aggregate plumbing cannot establish that every lender is safe; nor can a historical institutional crisis establish that aggregate dollar funding is currently scarce.

## A falsifiable next test

The observable test arrives with the 2026-08-27 $266B settlement and the 2026-08-31 $183B settlement.

The calendar-tightening thesis weakens if those windows pass while SOFR remains below IORB, Standing Repo Facility use remains not in size, and broader market-stress measures do not confirm pressure. In that outcome, the warning remains a structural and calendar signal rather than an observed funding event.

The thesis gains credibility only if the gap closes in observable behavior: overnight funding changes relative to IORB, the backstop is used in size, or market-stress measures confirm the pressure. Even then, that would describe system conditions. It would not identify the lenders whose balance sheets are vulnerable.

## Follow the pressure chain

Begin with the [Seiche daily dispatch](https://seiche.info/dispatches/2026-08-23-daily) and [Seiche methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology). They distinguish observed inputs, deterministic synthesis, and reserve-path scenarios in the system dollar-funding read.

At the system layer, follow reserves, foreign RRP, Treasury settlement dates, SOFR relative to IORB, and Standing Repo Facility usage through Seiche’s [series index](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json). At the lender layer, the relevant question is whether deposits, asset duration, collateral capacity, and funding access can withstand a cash call. At the market layer, the relevant question is whether crowding and exit capacity change the ability to turn assets into cash.

The March 2023 sequence shows how those layers can diverge: confidence can affect deposits; deposits can expose balance-sheet mismatches; and balance-sheet pressure can drive market repricing while system support is functioning.

## Sources, method, and limits

This replay uses the supplied Seiche dispatch, the [Seiche data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json), and [Seiche methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology). The composite is a Seiche derivation, not an observed market price. Source publication time is not yet collected uniformly, so event, desk-knowledge, and publication clocks remain separate.

**Research boundary:** Seiche covers system dollar-funding capacity. LiquiLens covers institution and lender balance-sheet risk. Undertow covers market liquidity, crowding, and exit capacity. Related Palimpsest readings are context-only and never enter the composite or a model feature.

The historical guide is desk-maintained background. Its engine comparison fields are construction point-in-time comparisons, not publication-vintage backtests or forecasts. Similarity is not recurrence. For continuing system monitoring, consult [Seiche dispatches](https://seiche.info/dispatches/); for the lender-level handoff, consult [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/); for the market-liquidity handoff, consult [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/).

# A high two-year yield meets a calendar-led dollar-funding strain call
Date: 2026-08-22 · Type: current_analysis · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-22-a-high-two-year-yield-meets-a-calendar-led-dollar-funding-strain-call/

The material new board change is the latest [two-year Treasury constant-maturity yield](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json) print: 4.19%, a 2.61-sigma level against its own history as of 2026-08-20. It raises a narrower question than the yield itself: is dollar-funding capacity tightening before the overnight cash market confirms it?

Seiche’s answer is guarded. Its composite reads 45.1, or STRAIN, but the dated reserve path—not current overnight pricing—carries the call. Scheduled Treasury settlements coincide with reserves that the fitted framework places below its estimated kink. That is a testable capacity concern, not evidence that present scarcity has already taken hold.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The proposed transmission path is dated settlement pressure meeting a lower reserve starting point. Seiche identifies $266.0B of Treasury settlement on 2026-08-27 and $183.0B on 2026-08-31. The relevant proposition is conditional: if those settlements meet limited capacity to absorb them, secured overnight funding could become more sensitive to the drain.

The fitted reserve-demand framework places reserves $768B below its estimated kink, with an R-squared of 0.62. That fit is context, not a precise threshold. Its implication is simply that the reserve base may have less room to absorb scheduled pressure before rates react.

The balance-sheet ledger provides the immediate backdrop. Reserves fell $8.8B in the week to 2026-08-19, to $2,935B. The foreign reverse-repo pool absorbed $16.0B and the balance sheet shrank $14.3B, while the residual released $10.9B. The six legs sum to the reserve change, though $8.0B of the balance-sheet move remains in the unnamed residual.

Foreign officials reduced Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B over 13 weeks while foreign reverse-repo parking rose by $55.6B. The combined official footprint still fell by $25.0B to $2,960B. Seiche calculates that 31% of the custody decline left the official sector rather than rotating within it. That is a changing official-sector footprint, not proof of a funding event.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

The 45.1 reading is a Seiche derivation, not an observed market price. Its largest contribution is the dated reserve path: the weather component is saturated at 100.0 and contributes 11.0 points. The reserve-kink component contributes 7.4 points. The decomposition matters because it explains why the regime reading is firmer than the live overnight tape.

For 2026-08-27, Seiche forecasts reserves of $2,947.9B and a worst-case reading of $2,894.8B alongside the $266.0B settlement. For 2026-08-31, the comparable figures are $2,946.2B and $2,879.7B alongside $183.0B of settlement. These are modelled reserve-path scenarios, not observed reserve prints.

The board also flags pressure dates on 2026-09-15, 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-30, with worst-case reserve readings of $2,842.2B, $2,814.7B and $2,779.5B. The calendar supplies dates for scrutiny; it does not establish that a disruption will occur.

The divergence between plumbing and price is the central contested signal. Seiche places plumbing at the 58th percentile of its own history and market stress at the 35th percentile, a 23.3 percentile-point gap described as “plumbing leads price.” That supports a watch for capacity pressure ahead of market pricing, but not a declaration of an active dollar-funding shortage.

A mid-month funding pop of 4.0 basis points is classified by Seiche as genuine scarcity. It should not dominate the evidence, however. For month-end, the forecast actually published is a naive 2.2-basis-point estimate, with a band of -1.8 to 6.9 basis points and severity of 1 on the stated calm-to-extreme scale. The model estimate of 9.6 basis points was not the published forecast.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis: overnight money still signals abundance. SOFR was 3.63% as of 2026-08-20, while IORB was 3.65% as of 2026-08-24. Seiche characterises the 0.9-basis-point gap below IORB as an abundance signal, not a scarcity print. EFFR was also 3.63% as of 2026-08-20.

The backstop is not being tested in size. Standing Repo Facility accepted take-up was $0.0B on 2026-08-21. Broader stress also remained at the 35th percentile of its own history, with the VIX at 16.01 and the high-yield option-adjusted spread at 2.75% as of 2026-08-20.

Those facts directly challenge the mechanism. If reserve scarcity is economically binding, secured funding should show it through the policy anchor or through meaningful recourse to the backstop. So far, it has not done so broadly. Seiche’s pooled five-business-day event read is 5.9%, while its underlying probability output does not outrank the rule-based index and is not to be read as literal odds.

## A falsifiable next test

The first clean test is the $266.0B settlement on 2026-08-27. The strain thesis gains support only if that scheduled pressure is followed by observable deterioration in secured funding relative to IORB, meaningful Standing Repo Facility use, or a broader rise in market-stress measures.

The thesis weakens materially if SOFR remains below IORB and the facility remains unused through the settlement window despite the projected reserve pressure. A benign 2026-08-31 month-end would provide a second disconfirmation, particularly against the published 2.2-basis-point, severity-1 path.

The calendar therefore supplies a pre-registered test rather than a prediction. The date identifies the proposed pressure point; the funding tape determines whether the mechanism is operating.

## Follow the pressure chain

Start with the scheduled Treasury settlement and the reserve path relative to the fitted kink. Then observe SOFR relative to IORB, Standing Repo Facility take-up, and whether broader market stress rises toward the plumbing signal.

The chain can fail at any link. The fitted kink may not identify a binding level; reserves may prove sufficient; or the settlement may pass without disorder in secured funding. Conversely, deterioration in secured funding without a comparable rise in broad market stress would support the narrower claim that plumbing is leading price.

## Research boundary

This article concerns Seiche’s remit: system dollar-funding capacity. [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/) covers institution and lender balance-sheet risk. [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/) covers market liquidity, crowding and exit capacity. Related Palimpsest readings are context only: they never enter the Seiche composite or a model feature.

Underlying public inputs and Seiche outputs are available through the [data overview](https://seiche.info/data/overview.json), [methodology](https://seiche.info/methodology), [series index](https://api.seiche.info/api/series/index.json), [daily dispatch](https://seiche.info/dispatches/2026-08-22-daily), and [dispatch archive](https://seiche.info/dispatches/). The composite is a deterministic synthesis of published point-in-time engines. Its confidence measure describes agreement across independent signals, not the probability of a market outcome.

The limits are central. The composite is not an observed market price. Source publication time is not yet collected uniformly, so event, desk-knowledge and publication clocks remain separate. The reserve-kink estimate is fitted, and the dated reserve paths are scenarios. Historical comparisons are context, not forecasts.

# Bitcoin’s jump is fresh; the dollar-funding warning still needs a cash-market confirmation
Date: 2026-08-21 · Type: current_analysis · Canonical: https://seiche.info/articles/2026-08-21-bitcoin-s-jump-is-fresh-the-dollar-funding-warning-still-needs-a-cash-ma/

Bitcoin’s Coinbase daily close rose $4,677.21 to $77,689.08, a 3.5-sigma move against its own history. It is the fresh market change in the latest dispatch. It does not, by itself, confirm tighter dollar funding.

Seiche’s board reads 45 out of 100, or STRAIN, because the dated reserve path is doing the work: reserves are below a fitted kink and Treasury settlements lie ahead. Current overnight pricing says something different. SOFR remains below IORB, the Standing Repo Facility is unused, and broad market stress is low. The evidence supports a pre-registered funding test, not a declaration that scarcity has arrived.

## The mechanism or historical setup

The proposed chain begins with reserves. The latest reserve reading was $2,935B, down $8.8B on the week. The ledger attributes a $16.0B absorption to the foreign RRP pool and a $14.3B balance-sheet contraction, partly offset by a $10.9B residual release. Its six legs sum to the reserve change to the dollar, though $8.0B of the balance sheet, or 0.12% of assets, remains in an unnamed residual.

The pressure is dated. A $266B Treasury auction settlement falls on Aug. 27 and a $183B settlement on Aug. 31. Seiche’s reserve path identifies both as pressure windows while reserves are below its estimated kink. The weather component is saturated at 100.0 and contributes 11.0 points to the composite, making the calendar the dominant driver.

That is a transmission hypothesis, not a mechanical rule that settlement cash must produce stress. The question is whether dated cash removal, against lower reserve buffers, raises the price at which dealers and lenders supply overnight capacity.

The bounded historical guide is the September 2025 tax-date squeeze, when a tax-date drain and Treasury settlement pressure briefly widened the gap between secured and unsecured overnight rates. Its value is methodological: specify the date and transmission path, then judge the funding tape. A calendar event is not itself a crisis signal.

## Quantified evidence with as-of context

At the latest reserve observation, the fitted reserve-demand kink was $3,702.8B, against reserves of $2,935.3B, a distance of -$767.5B. The fit’s R-squared is 0.616. This is a structural estimate, not an observed market-clearing threshold.

For Aug. 27, the reserve path estimates $2,942.7B of reserves and a worst-case $2,881.4B around the $266.0B settlement. For Aug. 31, it estimates $2,941.0B and a worst-case $2,870.0B around the $183.0B settlement. These are Seiche scenarios, not observed reserve prints.

Foreign officials cut Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose $55.6B. The combined official footprint nevertheless fell $25.0B to $2,960B: 31% of the custody decline left the official sector rather than rotating within it.

The divergence is notable but incomplete. Plumbing stands at the 58th percentile of its own history, market pricing at the 29th percentile: plumbing leads price by 30 percentile points. The pooled five-business-day event read is 6.4%, while a separate model read is 2.6%. Neither is a literal probability: the model does not beat climatology on probability levels.

## The strongest counter-case

The counter-case can defeat the thesis because it is based on the market that should react first. At the latest secured-rate observation, SOFR was 3.62%, 0.9bp below IORB; IORB was 3.65% at its latest observation. EFFR was 3.63%. A secured overnight rate below the administered reserve rate is an abundance signal, not a broad scarcity print.

Nor is the official backstop being tested. Standing Repo Facility accepted take-up was $0.00B at its latest observation. Market stress was at the 29th percentile of its history. VIX was 14.89 and the high-yield option-adjusted spread was 2.73%.

The board’s own month-end output is restrained. For Aug. 31, the published forecast is 2.2bp, within a band of -1.8bp to 6.9bp, with severity at 1 on its calm-to-extreme scale. The model estimate is 9.0bp, but the published estimate is the naïve one. If the funding tape does not change, this evidence outweighs a calendar-led strain call.

## A falsifiable next test

Aug. 27 is the first observable test: $266B settles while reserves sit below the estimated kink. Confirmation requires independent cash-market evidence that secured funding is becoming less abundant: SOFR moving toward or above IORB, meaningful Standing Repo Facility use, or a broader increase in the market-stress reading.

The thesis fails this test if SOFR remains below IORB, facility take-up remains negligible, and risk measures stay contained through the settlement window. The Aug. 31 $183B settlement supplies a second test. The point of dated tests is to make the claim gradeable rather than rhetorical.

Bitcoin’s move is not that confirmation. It is a fresh market signal; the funding argument stands or falls on overnight cash plumbing.

## Follow the pressure chain

The working sequence is reserve reduction; a below-kink estimate; Treasury settlement and calendar demands; potentially less dealer and lender balance-sheet elasticity; then a secured-rate response. The earlier links are observed inputs or Seiche derivations. The later links are the causal proposition under test.

Seiche covers system dollar-funding capacity. It does not convert a reserve-path scenario into a trade instruction. Institution and lender balance-sheet risk belongs with [LiquiLens](https://liquilens.in/); market liquidity, crowding, and exit capacity belong with [Undertow](https://liquilens-undertow.com/) and its [exit-capacity work](https://liquilens-undertow.com/exit/).
